name: Elrus
slug: Elrus is Walker's hidden ally in the coming confrontation.
description: Elrus is an ally of Walker who has agreed to accompany him when asked.

log.summary: Walker plans to bring Elrus to The Reach to scout the Dragon Rider training grounds. Walker has promised Elrus a place to stay and considers him a secret weapon who should remain unknown to the lich until the eventual confrontation. Walker expects Elrus to fight Grixto if they encounter him, though he worries Elrus may not hold back. Before departing, Elrus wished the party fruitful ventures and hoped their next meeting would allow them to vanquish their common foe.
notes: Walker stated that he needs to take Elrus somewhere.
Walker has promised Elrus a place to stay.
Elrus is willing to accompany Walker because Walker had previously asked him to come along.
Walker believes Elrus would probably become involved in a fight if they encountered Grixto.

Elrus is expected to be capable of confronting Grixto alongside Walker if they encounter him, though Walker worries Elrus may not hold back.

log.summary: Elrus travels with Walker and Plymouth toward the Dragon Rider training grounds, having earlier advised that dragon flight from Last Word Chasm to the site takes about five days. He cannot relieve Walker's daily exhaustion, avoids supply runs in Sunder, and helps teach Walker rudimentary fire signals before the group splits. Elrus then flies into the mountains with Araden, planning to rendezvous with the others later.
notes: Previously told Walker that flight from Last Word Chasm to the training grounds takes about five days.

log.summary: With Araden, Elrus helped end Grixto's group after Grixto killed the guild dragons at the training grounds. He travels with Walker to the training island and speaks into Walker's mind while the wind howls. He identifies the crumbled structure as the guild hall and suspects Grixto's cavern is reached from the backside or underneath. He offers to enter the crack or act as a relay, then stays outside as the relay. Because flag signals need line of sight, he tells Walker to call mentally, and says he can intervene faster than Araden, who would take a long time to dig the crevice open. When Walker contacts him from inside, he asks if Walker is in trouble. He says there has not been a trainee in centuries, that only one person used this place, that he did not know it was there until the vision Walker's friend presented, and that nothing dead should be down there. He agrees to get Plymouth and come down shortly.
notes: With Araden, he brought about the end of Grixto's group after Grixto killed the guild dragons at the training grounds.

log.summary: In Reach legend Elrus killed Galixtar as a trainer without his own legends, contemporary with Garixto the Betrayer, and later a legendary dragon rider. Carlkin does not remember if he was elf or human; some versions say he is still around. Walker called him in; he scrambled down the passage, said nothing to Vecna, with his sword in his belt, stared him down, and kept a side eye on him while leaving. Vecna took him for another of Walker's comrades. Elrus does not want Walker dealing with Vecna and calls the sister story morbid. He reads the four wall carvings as tilted cardinal views from the old central tower, cites mountains about ten and twenty-five degrees off, attributes them to Grixto's faulty memory, and cannot fit the angles to one vantage. He leads Walker from the cavern up a winding half-path across the plains to his and Grixto's ruined guild stronghold. He confirms madness is the most common outcome when a dragon or rider dies, and that he would then seek a book to bring the other back. He treats Walker's Galixtar theory as a real motive for the Al Kurin, better than most he has heard.
notes: In Reach legend he killed Galixtar. At the time he was a trainer without legends of his own, in the same era as Garixto the Betrayer, and he later became a legendary dragon rider. Carlkin does not remember whether he was elf or human. Some versions say he is still around.

Walker told him to come in. He is heard scrambling down the passage. During the talk with Vecna he says nothing, stands with his sword in his belt, and stares Vecna down, then keeps a side eye on him while leaving. Vecna takes him for another of Walker's comrades. He does not want Walker to deal with Vecna and calls the sister story morbid.

Reads the four wall carvings as local cardinal views from the old central tower, each slightly tilted, as if the artist had shifted location while standing in the same spot. He cites mountains about ten and about twenty-five degrees off, attributes the carvings to Grixto working from a faulty memory, and cannot make the angles fit one vantage.

Leads Walker from the cavern up a winding half-path, across the plains, to the ruined guild stronghold of his and Grixto's past. He confirms that madness is the most common outcome when a dragon or its rider dies, and that in that state he himself would seek a book to bring the other back. He treats Walker's theory about Galixtar as a real motive for the Al Kurin, better than most theories he has heard.

log.summary: Elrus is shadowing Walker in the cave and confirms it. He names the grassy atoll, Mount Elcastar, and Monkey Falls with its old obsidian ley-line marker, and teaches Walker the Weave and ley lines, saying Walker's training must speed up or he will never beat Grixto. He has visited only a few convergences and may go to this one if other business stalls. The marker Viablis has stood since he was a boy; he reads the clockwise rotation as Grixto moving the old intersection to a convergence Grixto has found. He does not know the exact lich ritual, treats the troop markers as toy soldiers, reads the eagle as a hobgoblin legion standard, and cannot explain the figurines without a map. When stuck he meditates, then coaches Walker for hours on nasal, diaphragm breathing so Walker can unweave rituals Grixto set for him. He is the one Walker has been trying to listen to. He sets the eagle on the square table, says the repeated action now makes sense and that the eagle has nothing to do with a mountain or a waterfall, then asks for the cavalry markers rather than the rams before the explanation is cut off. He assembled the table, reads the hunched eagle and troop tokens as a landmark map of Grixto's plan, and concludes they are in over their heads. He confirms the fifteen-degree obelisk offset means a conveyance and that wards are amplified only nearby. He once carried energy gems like Walker's and gave them to other prospective riders long ago. He can describe primal stones and offers to try condensing Walker's energy into them, with the risk that Walker loses part of himself into the stone, but wants more meditation before Walker channels.

log.summary: Elrus, the dragonrider instructing Walker, advised the convergence that lights the map. His Nyx table offers more information or another gold eagle; cave markers were generic. He can help Walker make primal stones, or a good roll may let Walker do it. Surprised he was not told, he has tried setting stones into objects and thinks Plymouth versatile enough. There is no time to get his equipment; he calls Walker a fledgling and says training is imminent. He does not know a cosmic loom, but could start carvings and procure pillar materials. At the obelisk the working needs no meditation, but Walker should meditate anyway. From a pebble, scorched moss, and an insect he casts a cantrip lighting about 60 feet, then 60 more. He postpones the real working and wants meditation, training, and magic practice before returning to Midgard. His watch reads 42 days; Walker has trained throughout and still needs more. He offers to imbue primal stones on the spot; Walker declines until talking with the party. At the stronghold he had framed training, not Grazog. When the forest beacon appears, Walker says the plan has changed. Elrus treats the disturbance as the companions, and they fly after Dana.
notes: He is the dragonrider instructing Walker. He advised the convergence because it lights up the map. His table in Nyx is a lead for more information or another gold eagle; the markers in the cave where he was living were generic.

He can help Walker make primal stones, and with a good enough roll Walker may be able to do it himself. He is surprised he was not told a convergence had been found. He has tried once or twice to set such stones into objects and thinks Plymouth may be versatile enough to do that setting.

He has none of his equipment with him and wants to circle back for it. He is told there is no time, calls Walker a fledgling, and says training is imminent. He does not know where a cosmic loom is. He could start the carvings and try to procure pillar materials, which would take time.

At the obelisk he says the working does not require meditation, but that Walker should meditate regardless. From a pebble, scorched moss, and an insect he casts a simple cantrip whose light reaches about 60 feet and then another 60 feet. He lacks the right equipment, postpones the real working, and wants meditation, training, and more magic practice at the site before a later return to Midgard.

His watch reads exactly 42 days. He says Walker has been training that whole time and still needs to train more. He offers to imbue primal stones on the spot. Walker declines until he talks with the party.

He is with Walker when they land at the stronghold. He had framed the next step as training instead of Grazog. When the forest beacon appears, Walker tells him the plan has changed. Elrus treats the disturbance as the companions, and he and Walker fly after Dana.
